Donald Trump Reportedly Told Staff He Won’t Leave the White House on January 20
Twitter users would be thrilled to see him dragged out.
By
Emily Tannenbaum
December 17, 2020
Pool/Getty Images
The Electoral College
confirmed
Joe Biden’s presidential win
on December 15; however, it seems
current president Donald Trump
is still unwilling to accept defeat.
After more than a month of fighting the results of the election by citing rampant voter fraud without a stitch of evidence,
CNN reports
Trump told staffers at one point he'd refuse to leave the White House on Inauguration Day, January 20, and had to be “walked down from that ledge.”
“He’s throwing a fucking temper tantrum,” one White House staffer said, per CNN. “He’s going to leave. He’s just lashing out.” Even if that’s true, is it any wonder the guy who said he was
“entitled”
to a third term in office is reportedly having a meltdown over leaving before a second?
Trump previously
promised to leave
the White House should the Electoral College confirm Joe Biden’s victory, although his statement came off less than reassuring. “Certainly I will, and you know that,” he replied to a reporter during his November
tiny-desk press conference
. “But I think there will be a lot of things happening between now and the 20th of January. A lot of things. Massive fraud has been found. We’re like a third-world country.”
When asked if he would attend the Biden inauguration, he replied, “I know the answer to that, but I don’t want to say it yet.”
The Biden campaign, however, does not seem too concerned about exchanging house keys with Donald Trump. “As we said on July 19th, the American people will decide this election,” Andrew Bates, a representative for Biden’s campaign,
said in a statement
on November 6. “And the United States government is perfectly capable of escorting trespassers out of the White House.”
Now that’s something people on Twitter would like to see. “Does the Secret Service or the National Guard need help dragging Trump out of the WH on January 20th?” one user asked.
